Twin Peaks Mountaineer is a player vs. player achievement earned for performing a /roar emote with the flag while under the effect of both a speed power up and the berserking power up in Twin Peaks.

.]] The Twin Monoliths are the two gigantic mogu statues located in the center of the Vale of Eternal Blossoms. They were built long ago by pandaren slaves of the mogu empire under the rule of the Thunder King. Between them once stood the Golden Pagoda which was destroyed when Garrosh Hellscream awakened the Sha of Pride. Feedback from the event destroyed not only the building, but the surrounding areas, heavily damaging the two statues. One of them had within it a secret door to the Pools of Power under Mogu'shan Palace. At some point later, the Vale of Eternal Blossoms was restored, but the colossal statues remained broken.

Uldis is a subzone of the Storm Peaks located far below the Temple of Storms, but still high on the mountain. The entrance is an aperture that's partially telescoped open, enough to easily fly a gryphon into, halfway up the mountain on the south side, located just north of Bor's Breath and southeast of Valkyrion. The interior is filled with titan machinery, resembling a giant engine room. During the the war against the Lich King, it was also the location of the Heart of the Storm, guarded by Overseer Narvir, until adventurers were sent by Bouldercrag the Rockshaper to take it, before the iron dwarves could use it for the construction of the Iron Colossus. After defeating certain bosses within, they become available to use by the players for the same purpose. They are the only way to advance into The Antechamber.

__NOTOC__ The Un'Goro Examinant is a titan orb that appears at Marshal's Stand after you have completed the The Eastern Pylon, The Northern Pylon and The Western Pylon to examine the pylons, and the quest Crystals of Power to gather the various colored crystals scattered around Un'Goro. It will inform you that the Watcher Nablya has requested your presence, and will teleport you to The Shaper's Terrace if you ask him. From than on it'll be at Marshal's Stand permanently, and will teleport you back to the Shaper's Terrace if you talk to him.

Uncorrupted warlocks are rare warlocks who do not suffer from arcane corruption: their alignments remain inviolate, unless they cast evil spells, and do evil deeds. Most young warlocks claim they know what they're getting into. They know about the seductive whisper of power and the strength of the Nether. They know of the crushing will of the demon lords and, most of all they know of the corruptive influence of warlock magic. They say it will not happen to them; they will not fall to evil, as have so many before them. Most of them are wrong. Most of them join the dark ranks of the creatures with which they traffic. An Undercity Gift Collection is a collection of the three Undercity pledge item packages, and is the second hierarchical combining of the pledge items given out by various Undercity NPCs during the Love is in the Air seasonal event. __NOTOC__

An Undercity Pledge Collection is a package of five pledge gifts, and is the first hierarchical combining of the pledge items given out by various Undercity NPCs during the Love is in the Air seasonal event. All of the Love is in the Air pledge gift packages are non-functional as regards their name and picture. You cannot read an Undercity Pledge Collection. __NOTOC__

Undercity Love Boats are small rowboats found circling the Canals in Undercity during the Love is in the Air event. They originate at a pier in the Apothecarium, circles the city, and ends at the pier just before the first one. All of these boats follow the same route. It is a clickable vehicle, designed for two players to board it. It can be boarded at any point, and can be left through the standard vehicle interface. Once the two players board it, a love heart forms above each of their heads. Upon returning to the dock, the boat despawns, and anyone still in the boat is returned to the dock.

Undercity Reveler are Forsaken located in the Ruins of Lordaeron above the Undercity and Moonglade during the Lunar Festival. They also appear in the Ruins of Lordaeron and Tirisfal Glades during the New Year and Midsummer Fire Festival firework events.

The Undertaker's Pass is a subterranean passage from a fishing shop in Greymane Court, in Gilneas City, that leads to Aderic's Repose outside the proper city. It goes under the Northgate River. It was used by the Gilneans to evacuate the city before the Forsaken blighted them during the invasion of Gilneas.
The Unfinished Star Chart was created from a Partial Star Chart. It could be turned into a Completed Star Chart with Medivh's Telescope.

Unstable Portal Shard is a reward from One Magical, Flying Kingdom's Trash... and can be subsequently purchased from for each. They can be planted at Sunsong Ranch to grow a random consumable Portal Shard that can be used to open a portal from Sunsong Ranch to a major faction city. Requires Revered with the Tillers.

The Unseen Path is an order of hunters, archers, rangers, beast masters, and trappers. It was founded on the Broken Isles by Namuria Gladesong after the War of the Ancients, and was blessed by the eagle spirit Ohn'ahra. When the elves who founded the Unseen Path left Mount Hyjal to return to the Broken Isles, the Highmountain tauren recognized the nobility of their cause and offered them friendship. It was the descendants of Huln Highmountain who led the Unseen Path to its peak. Since the Burning Legion's return, the Highmountain have helped restore the lodge, such as replacing two damaged watch towers with tauren structures. Unstable Rift Crystal used to be the "shortcut" entrance to Molten Core in Blackrock Mountain. It used to be located left of Lothos Riftwaker. It existed as an alternative to the window shortcut added in patch 1.3.0. It was only usable if one had completed the quest Attunement to the Core, the attunement quest for Molten Core. When Lothos Riftwaker gained the ability to teleport players himself in patch 1.11.0, the crystal was removed.

They are immensely strong and tough, and focus on improving their natural, bearlike natures. They disembowel dragons with their claws and crush small creatures that come within their grasp. These creatures achieve a higher level of power and feral grace; many think that ursa totemics are infused with the power of the twin bear demigods (Ursoc and Ursol). Urefu is a giraffe and is one of many animals featured in the Darkmoon Faire zoo on Darkmoon Island. Urefu shares a spawn location within the same corral as Mabaka and Shingo.

__NOTOC__ The Valley of Spears is a valley in western Desolace where the Maraudine clan of centaur make their home. The entrance to Maraudon is located in the southwestern end of the valley. Besides the countless centaur, one can also find the captive Melizza Brimbuzzle here. On foot, the valley is only accessible through narrow mountain passes in the south and east. The Cataclysm destroyed the northern wall of the valley (though this is too steep to climb from the outside) and opened up a shortcut through the southern mountain pass.

Vanish is a rogue ability allows a rogue to disappear from sight, entering an improved stealth mode for 3 seconds even while in combat. During that time damage and harmful effects will not break stealth, but they will still afflict the rogue. Once the Vanish buff has worn off, the rogue will still be in standard Stealth. Upon being cast, Vanish also breaks any movement impairing effects. In addition to escaping, Vanish can be used as a damage cooldown, especially when the Subterfuge talent is chosen, as well as a powerful PvP cooldown allowing the rogue to briefly "pause" combat and then repeat an opening attack sequence.

Veil Terokk is the home the Arakkoa Outcasts, a collection of broken and flightless arakkoa who revere and the ancient king , for whom the veil is named, and use shadow magic to combat the fire and wind of Rukhmar's flying arakkoa followers, the Adherents of Rukhmar. Veil Terokk is shrouded from the Adherents, likely by an illusion spell which the Outcasts often use.

The Veiled Ossuary is a repository for the bones of dragons, located on an island north of the Algeth'ar Academy in Thaldraszus. It was originally built to house and memorialize dead dragons. An artifact originally held by the Keeper Tyr was hidden here, and sought after by both the Dragonscale Expedition and the Sundered Flame. The blue dragonflight had a vault in the Ossuary for their own dead; those who could return to the Dragon Isles after Neltharion's betrayal were laid to rest there. Senegos was the last remaining gravekeeper by this time. When the dragonflights could not return to the Isles after the War of the Ancients, they used the Dragonblight in Northrend as their final resting

Vermillion Redoubt is a Red dragonflight outpost in the Twilight Highlands. It is centered around a large red tree. Several red dragons and red dragonspawn can be found here, many of them fighting the Twilight Dragonflight and Twilight's Hammer. The area also contains a few shallow ponds where schools of Highland Guppy can spawn. During the Fourth War, void-twisted twilight dragonflight led by Vexiona attacked the Redoubt. Aided with Kalecgos and an adventurer, the Vermillion dragons led by Alexstrasza defended the area and drove the invaders away.

The Verdant Wilds is an Island Expedition in Battle for Azeroth. It is a forested island with a few ruins that teems with Spirit, the element of life. It is inhabited by Cenarius's children, furbolgs and druidic peoples. The local keepers of the grove, dryads, and druids do not see others as allies. They seek to preserve the balance above all things, even if that means unaware adventurers' deaths. The druids are those who, after the War of the Satyr, came to believe that at their core they were wild creatures, their humanoid forms were merely a guise. They left night elven society for this island.
Verdant Gladiator: Dragonflight Season 3 is a feat of strength achievement earned by ending Dragonflight PvP Season 3 in the top 0.1% of the 3v3 arena ladder.
Verdant Legend: Dragonflight Season 3 is a feat of strength achievement earned by ending Dragonflight PvP Season 3 in the top 0.1% of the Solo Shuffle ladder.
Vestia Moonspear is a night elf quest giver originally found at the original Feathermoon Stronghold in Feralas, now located at the Tower of Estulan. Her husband was Latronicus Moonspear.

__NOTOC__ Vhel'kur is an undead black dragon flying in an endless circle above Netherwing Ledge in southeastern Shadowmoon Valley. According to the Ancient Shadowmoon Spirit, Vhel'kur is a "spawn of Deathwing" who called the ledge his home in life until he was killed by Teron Gorefiend. Vhel'kur's titanic skeleton remains on the Netherwing Ledge (apparently where Gorefiend slew him). He can be ranged pulled from one of the hills on the Ledge, but he lands very quickly, and it is advisable to have a tank ready to pick him up. Spectrecles are required to see or damage him.
Vibroblade is a random drop from all trash mobs in Gnomeregan. It has the ability to lower the target's armor. It is a possible reference to the Star Wars Universe, where swords Vibroblades are used.

The Violet Gate is the entrance to the city of Dalaran via the teleport crystal from Violet Stand in Crystalsong Forest. Archmage Celindra, Dalaran's portal trainer, is located in a room directly below the Gate, as is the teleport crystal to return to the surface.

Void gods are a powerful type of void creature and the end result of a naaru losing its light. They are evil creatures of the Void and capable of destroying entire planets if left unchecked. Several of the void gods that have so far been seen were created when the light of a naaru was forcibly drained from it, with the rest near K'ara, so they may not be a natural occurrence. A void god can be turned back into a naaru through great effort, as seen with Saraka and Saa'ra. The rune Igannok is one of the many marks of the Void Gods, and using it is said to beckon their attention to you. Void Ray is a Demonology warlock ability, available at level 85. It replaces Fel Flame (warlock ability) while in Metamorphosis (warlock ability).
Wake Up is a level 10 hunter ability that commands the hunter's pet to wake up from Play Dead (hunter ability). This ability is taught by Pet Training Manual: Play Dead.

WarChasers is a scenario map for Warcraft III made by Blizzard Entertainment. Four daring souls choose from a gallery of fallen heroes and fight their way through a legendary city against overwhelming masses of monsters! — Warcraft III The souls chose from eight heroes of The Age of Legends. The souls used the heroes to fight monsters of the Soulless in order to redeem the heroes' eternal souls. They fought through multiple levels of the city, even being transported to hell — spending time there — and having to fight the forces there before they could escape back to the city. The night elves developed along the shores of the Well of Eternity, and so they were strengthened by its energies. Despite the trolls’ attempts to keep this new race from claiming further territories, the night elves built up a mighty empire that expanded rapidly across Kalimdor. Wielding fierce magics never before imagined by the trolls, the night elves soon threatened the two greatest empires on Azeroth, the Amani and Gurubashi Empires. The night elves systematically dismantled the troll’s defenses and supply chains. Unable to counter the elves’ destructive magics, the trolls buckled under the onslaught. The territories of the Gurubashi and Amani empires fragmented within only a few years,

The war against the Zandalari broke out in the period following the Cataclysm, when Zandalar, the home island of the Zandalar tribe, was destroyed in the aftermath and out of desperation the Zandalari moved to take advantage of the chaos by joining the tribes into a mighty troll empire. When the mists surrounding Pandaria vanished the Zandalari quickly sent aid to their ancient allies and former rulers of the continent, the mogu empire. The ultimate goal on Pandaria seems to be establishing themselves a new homeland.

Warchief's Command Boards can be found at any major Horde quest hub in Azeroth. It offers level-appropriate quests for all zones. The quests offered are specific to their continent--that is, to see available Kalimdor zones, one must visit the Orgrimmar board, and for Eastern Kingdoms, the Undercity one. The equivalent billboard for the Alliance is the Hero's Call Board, an example of which can be found between the bank and the auction house in the Trade District of Stormwind City. While the quests posted on the board are not required and are merely breadcrumb quests, they are intended to help players who either do not know where to quest at their level or are simply ready for the next stage

The Warchief's Fist was an Horde destroyer stationed off the coast of Tanaris and captained by Aldrek. Under Aldrek's command, the Warchief's Fist was on a reconnaissance mission for the upcoming battle against Theramore. The Warchief's Fist was ultimately destroyed when Talithar Swiftwind, chose to assist Chen Stormstout and Baenan in their escape attempt by detonating all the gunpowder ammunition for the ship's cannons in the munitions hold with his fire-based magic. Talithar went down with the ship, as it were, and Chen and Baenan were successfully able to escape.
Warlock abilities are abilities that warlocks use. Most abilities are shared between all specializations, while some are only available to one (or two) specializations.

Warden Jor'al was a nightborne construct located in Suramar. He guarded a large amount of Lumenstones as nightborne were transporting them to the city. Right before it could get cover behind the walls of Suramar City, he was destroyed when the Silver Hand came looking for the Lumenstone.
Warrior abilities are abilities used by warriors. Most abilities are available to all specializations, while some are specific to one (or two) specializations.

The Warrior's Terrace (also referred to as the Hall of Justice) is a major central district in the night elf capital city of Darnassus, serving as a base for the city's warrior trainers, battlemasters, and the Sentinels. Most night elves of military status utilized the training areas here to hone their skills. There they had the use of target ranges and dueling grounds. It occupies the easternmost section of Darnassus, located at the main gate leading out into the greater Teldrassil region. The district protects Darnassus from violent incursions. Warspear Shaman are tauren found in Warspear Outpost in Ashran, assisting Atomik in the empowerment of the Underpowered Earth Fury. With enough power, they will transform it into the Earth Fury Kronus, who will do battle for the Horde.

Wasteland Propriety is a soulbind trait available on row 8 of Theotar the Mad Duke's soulbind tree. It causes your Venthyr class ability to grant you and your allies a temporary versatility bonus. The buff lasts 1/6 the time of your Venthyr class ability's cooldown. Since the warrior ability Condemn has no cooldown, warriors have a line added to Wasteland Propriety's tooltip: "You may only serve tea every 1 min." The buff lasts 10 seconds to match.

The Waygate is a portal between the southern part of Sholazar Basin and the Shaper's Terrace in Un'Goro Crater. It is of titan craft and arcane power, and a piece of titan technology that is still active makes a pillar of light into a magical portal. As the twin of a machine in Un'Goro Crater, this waygate hasn't been active in seven centuries, but can be activated using the switches found in the Makers' Overlook and the Makers' Perch. The gate then becomes active and will teleport anyone to Un'Goro in an instant. Following the war against the Jailer, the brothers Bronzebeard visited the waygate and learned how to use it. When used, the Weather-Beaten Journal teaches the player Find Fish, the ability to observe fishing spots on the mini-map in the same manner as the herbalist's ability to see herb nodes. This is the only way to gain the ability.

The Wayward Landing is where the Alliance fleet and, later, a squadron of bombers crashes after being attacked by the Horde. The Landing is located in the far southwest of the Jade Forest upon the Silken Shore and borders the Veridian Grove. The Alliance fleet was successful in rescuing the "White Pawn" from the Horde, but were then pursued and fired upon. In the ensuing naval battle, they were forced to enter dense fog for cover, fog that surrounded the continent of Pandaria. Admiral Taylor managed to get off one garbled transmission to Stormwind City. In response, Stormwind sends a flight of stealth bombers. The bombers also encounter the Horde and are fired upon, crashing in the same area
The Westrift is a fjord which separates the rest of the Borean Tundra from the mountainous island of Coldarra. A broken bridge spans the Westrift into the nearby island.

Welcome Bear refers jokingly to the higher level bears that roam the Western Plaguelands. The joke is that new undead players, not knowing that Western Plaguelands is a much higher level zone than the adjacent Tirisfal Glades where they begin, wander in from the relatively safe Tirisfal Glades and are horribly murdered by — usually — a Diseased Black Bear. Hence, the Welcome Bear. One variant is the "Welcome Spider", another recurring Plaguelands mob. The Welcome Bear is also experienced by people who try to travel on foot from Tirisfal Glades to Ghostlands or Silvermoon City without realizing they could just take the Orb of Translocation from Undercity. Werewolves, or lycanthropes, are humanoids that can shapeshift into a wolf or wolf-like creature. Werewolves have a vulnerability to silver. The runic spell "mark of the werewolf" imbues a caster with the essence of a werewolf including its vulnerabilities. Some humans transform into lycanthropic worgen when the moon rises due to the worgen curse.

Westfall is an Alliance-only level 10-15 zone in western Azeroth of the Eastern Kingdoms. Players are led here from Elwynn Forest and are immediately thrust into a murder mystery case. The storyline takes players around the broken zone and into the Deadmines before returning to Sentinel Hill for the climax. The progress of the storyline is tracked in the achievement Westfall Quests. After Threat to the Kingdom, or as soon as players reach level 14, players are sent to Three Corners in Redridge Mountains to start the Redridge Mountains storyline with Hero's Call: Redridge Mountains! (NPC).
Welcome to the Darkmoon Races is the tutorial quest for the Darkmoon Races at the Darkmoon Faire.

The Wetlands is a large, wet zone below Stonewrought Dam and north of Loch Modan, covered with small rivers, lakes, and ponds. Bordered on three sides by mountains, the Wetlands are open to the ocean to the west. Adventurers seeking a route to the Wetlands must either come through sieged Dun Algaz from Loch Modan or cross the damaged Thandol Span from Arathi Highlands. The northern slopes of Wetlands are generally classed within mountains of Khaz Modan. The Wetlands is a vast, cold swamp. Mists cloak the ground, and the overcast sky makes the land a uniform gray. Whisperwind Moonwell Water is obtained by filling the Empty Moonwell Vial with the waters of the moonwell at the center of Whisperwind Grove in Felwood.

__NOTOC__ Wickerman Guardians are abominations guarding the Wickerman Festival outside Undercity during Hallow's End. They are Horde guards, and will attack approaching Alliance players trying to complete the quest Crashing the Wickerman Festival. They have a powerful melee attack and Chain Hook ability as well as a disease cloud aura.
Widget is a house cat located in the Darkmoon Faire on Darkmoon Island, sitting behind Jeremy Feasel on a stand with Gizmo.

The Wild Overlook is a cliff on the northeastern side of the small island of the Lost Isles overlooking the larger island. It is from here the goblins and orcs travel to the larger island. The Savage Glen can be found just west of here.

The wildkin are serene, powerful creatures, believed by the night elves and tauren to have been created by the moon goddess Elune to protect her sacred places. They look like a cross between a bear and a horned owl, which explains both their wisdom and ferocity, and they possess all the best traits of Elune's beloved night birds and the brute force of the benevolent bears. Wildkin have long been allies of the night elves, helping to protect their sacred sites. Though they are thoughtful creatures, wildkin harbor a particular hatred for the Burning Legion and the Scourge, recognizing the danger they pose. Will of the Forsaken is an undead racial trait which removes any Charm, Fear, or Sleep effect. The ability does not remove the horrify from Death Coil or deep slumber effects such as during the Mograine event in Scarlet Monastery. The ability is a similar but more limited version of Will to Survive, but unlike that ability does not full share a cooldown with Faction Insignia trinkets (as of Patch 3.3.)

.]] Wilderlings (or wolf serpents) are benevolent and magical flying creatures of Ardenweald. They have sinuous fur-covered bodies with antlered wolf heads and are drawn to strong, pure souls. In battle, they act as support units by preserving their allies and disabling enemy magics. When anima once again began flowing to Ardenweald's distant forests, the wilderlings cautiously emerged from their canopy burrows.

Wind Trader Lathrai is a engineering vendor located in the Lower City of the neutral Shattrath City. He deals in exotic goods from other dimensions. He sold the parts used to build the mana bomb that destroyed the Cenarion Thicket to the merchant Empoor.
Windtamer Nalt is a Highmountain tauren flight master located at Thunder Totem in Highmountain.

Winglord's Perch is a set of two islands off the northwestern shore of Forbidden Reach. The islands are inhabited by Vorquin, Vorquin Foals, and Wild Ohuna. The battle pet world quest Cutting Wind takes place here when Vortex spawns. A few Storm-Touched Swoglets are present as well. A Dragon Glyph is inside the smaller broken tower on the big island.

The witches of the Heartsbane Coven are humans from Drustvar who have been empowered by the Drust. They are led by the matrons. The death magic they wield has contorted their bodies. When a witch grows powerful enough, they slit their own throats to ascend.

The Withering Thicket is a small stretch of forest found north of the Ruins of Auberdine in Darkshore. It was broken off from the rest of the mainland during the Cataclysm, and is now an island bordered by rapids to the north, south, and east, and ocean to the west. Moonstalkers are commonly found here. Keeper Karithus and Seraphine are located here as well. Parts of the Withering Thicket were cut down by the Horde after the War of the Thorns. The cleared area was used by them to hold night elven prisoners. Some prisoners were used as target practice. Ivus the Forest Lord eventually moved here to assist the elven effort at retaking Darkshore.

The Woodpaw Hills is a forest in southeastern Feralas. It's here the gnolls of the Woodpaw clan make their home, however, they're being driven out by the "bugs" that have burst through the ground in the southeasternmost area of the hills in an area now called the Writhing Deep. Recently mountain giants have arrived in the area, although Mountain Giant Muisek (quest) states they came down from the mountains to aid the night elves when the Burning Legion attacked. These giants, unlike the Cliff Giants in the west are hostile to the Horde. The Woodpaw Alphas that lead the tribe were once found in the camps, they can now be found only in the Woodpaw Den.

Wounded Highmountain Protectors are Highmountain tauren guards found at Thunder Totem in Highmountain during the Assault on Thunder Totem.

The Wrathtail are naga lurking on the northwestern coast of Ashenvale, known as the Zoram Strand. It is the resting place of the doomed city of Zoram, destroyed during the Great Sundering and submerged beneath the seas. It has been lost to the night elves for ages. Lost, and nearly forgotten. Now, the naga have returned, and for what reason is unknown. The naga honor the wicked nature of a hydra, Vorsha the Lasher, with a brazier that remains lit on an island just off the coast.

Wrathion, the Black Prince, is one of the few black dragons on Azeroth known to be uncorrupted by the taint of the Old Gods and, following the death of Deathwing and the destruction of the corrupted black dragonflight, one of the last known black dragons alive on Azeroth. Claiming to have seen a future where Azeroth falls, Wrathion helped heroes of the Horde and Alliance gaining powers, usually in the form of magical legendary items. He is, however, ruthless in his goals and pursues what he perceives as the greater good for Azeroth with almost fanatical devotion. The invasion of Dalaran was an attack on the Magocracy of Dalaran orchestrated by Xal'atath and the kingdom of Azj-Kahet. The invasion occurred shortly after Dalaran was teleported to Khaz Algar, resulting in the destruction of the floating city by the Dark Heart, the disappearance of Khadgar, and the deaths of numerous civilians. Most survivors were either teleported to safety on the Isle of Dorn or taken captive by the nerubians and brought to the depths of Azj-Kahet. The destruction of Dalaran marked the beginning of the war in Khaz Algar and the first step in the Harbinger's plan to claim Azeroth's worldsoul.
